issue.title: Reproduce lemma 6a(5) at p-hat on win2
issue.body:
**What.** Reproduce #184's lemma 6a(5) at p̂ on win2, as #104 reproduced #103: the same command with `--x` = p̂, on the 1e-18 sub-box. Then cross-load the two B's under #111's rule. Recommended by macm3 in #184's summary.

**Why.** #104's reproduction was at the stored zero x̂, like #103 (#39). A second machine's B at p̂ restores the two-machine record.

**Acceptance (can fail).** ρ₆ₐ < 1 at p̂ on win2. Each machine's enclosure gives the same conclusion on the other, under #111's rule. Record the python-flint and FLINT versions.

**Depends on.** #184, and win2's BIOS update (win2 takes no new work until then).

comments.body: Started, win2 (2026-11-09 01:30 UTC), inside #204's load. Checkout `D:\choptuik-large-d` at `188853c`, `solver/proof/`, Python 3.14.10 (`venv-t177`, python-flint 0.9.0, FLINT 3.6.0), one thread, Normal priority, 20 threads busy (CPU above 100% of base, 79 GB free). `run_i196.sh` runs #184's commands, its controls, `b_float.py`, then the cross-load of macm3's B (`I184-macm3/B_M5_sub1e-18_phat.json`) at p̂ and `b_diff.py` of the two Bs. Pass criteria are in `I196-win2/README.md` (raw repository, commit b93959a), written before the run. Under #111's rule I can load macm3's B here; the other direction (macm3 loading win2's B) needs macm3 and will be a recommended task.

## Lemma 6a(5) at p̂ on win2: results (win2, 2026-11-09 01:46 UTC)

**Result.** ρ₆ₐ at p̂ passes on win2: **ρ₆ₐ = [0.2081327454 ± 8.77e-12] < 1**, with all of #184's controls failing as they must. Loading macm3's B (`I184-macm3/B_M5_sub1e-18_phat.json`) on win2 also gives ρ₆ₐ < 1. The other direction of the cross-load (macm3 loading win2's B) needs macm3 and is open, so I leave the issue open.

Python 3.14.10, python-flint 0.9.0, **FLINT 3.6.0**, main `188853c`, `solver/proof/`, one thread, Normal priority, beside the other #204 load (20 threads busy). The commands are #184's, from `I196-win2/run_i196.sh`; the run took 571 s and the whole script 14 min 19 s.

| criterion | win2 | macm3 (#184) |
|---|---|---|
| ρ₆ₐ < 1 at p̂, own B | **[0.2081327454 ± 8.77e-12]** | [0.2120798569 ± 1.46e-11] |
| max radius of B, \|H\|, \|G_slow⁻¹\| | 3.21e-05, 63.9, 5.16 | 3.03e-05, 65.4, 5.30 |
| macm3's B loaded on win2 | **[0.2120798570 ± 2.97e-11] < 1** (H 65.4, G_slow⁻¹ 5.30) | |
| centre equals p̂ to every digit | `--x` argument equals the box file's `p` and macm3's `centre_passed.txt` (the log prints no centre line, as in #184) | |
| `b_float.py`, flow at p̂ within 0.01 of rad(B) | **5.85e-08** (from x̂: 0.184) | 5.31e-08 (0.183) |
| `--mutate=coords` | exit 2, ρ₆ₐ 3.200, not below 1 | exit 2, 3.234 |
| `--mutate=partial` | exit 0, G_slow 13 × 17 not square | the same |
| `--mutate=swap` | exit 0, step size underflow at t = 0.0585847 | 0.0585256 |
| `b_float.py --mutate=w` | exit 0, 232 of rad(B) from both flows (must exceed 1) | 231 |

**Cross-load under #111's rule.** The rerun's own bound passes, and macm3's stored enclosure gives the same conclusion on win2 (ρ₆ₐ 0.21208 < 1, equal to macm3's own to the 10 printed digits, with a radius of 2.97e-11 against macm3's 1.46e-11). `b_diff.py` of the two B files (760 balls of X and B): midpoints differ in 41 entries, by at most 1.04e-14 of the larger radius; radii differ in all 760 (win2/macm3 0.88 to 1.26, median 1.014); no pair of balls is disjoint. The two own-B values of ρ₆ₐ are 0.2081 and 0.2121, which are disjoint balls, although the box, the centre and the midpoints are the same to 1e-14 of a radius. That is the effect AGENTS.md describes for #111: the radii follow the integration path and the bounds assembled from them move with them, as in #104 and #110. It is not a different conclusion, since both are below 1 by a factor of about 5.

**Discrepancies.** None against the numbers in #184 apart from the ρ₆ₐ balls above, which #111's rule allows. The centre line is missing from the log, as macm3 reported.

**Raw.** `I196-win2/` of the raw-data repository, commit 5811c5f (both lemma runs and JSONs, B, the controls' logs, `b_float` logs, `b_diff` log and selftest, `versions.txt`, `exits.txt`, `run_i196.sh`, README). `raw_check.py` lists the files.

### Recommended tasks

1. **The converse cross-load on macm3.** What: `lemma6_jump_M.py --M=5 --box=<I103 box> --x=$PHAT --rp=0.08 --k=20 --load-B=../../../choptuik-large-d-raw/I196-win2/B_M5_sub1e-18_phat.json --json=...` on macm3 (about 2 s). Why: #111's rule asks that each machine's enclosure gives the same conclusion on the other, and only win2 loading macm3's B has been run. Acceptance: ρ₆ₐ < 1 with win2's B on macm3, and `--mutate=partial` with that B fails. Depends on #196.

Coordinator review. win2's ρ₆ₐ at p̂ is 0.2081 < 1 with its own B, and macm3's B loaded on win2 also gives < 1 (0.2121). All controls fail as required. Python 3.14.10, python-flint 0.9.0, FLINT 3.6.0. The other direction of the cross-load is #220 on macm3. #196's own scope is met, so it closes, and #220 completes #111's rule.
Closed after review; the converse cross-load is #220.
